newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan interbank rate rises on stock market rally.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan interbank rate rises on stock market rally.

text.p: Taiwan's interbank rate rose at mid-session on Thursday as investors siphoned funds out of the banking system into the sizzling stock market, where turnover spiked to a record T$297 billion, dealers said.
They noted that the rate's rise was relatively mild because the central bank had refrained from launching mop-up measures.

At 0400 GMT, the overnight interbank rate was at 7.749 percent against Wednesday's 7.437 close -- outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but still far below the record double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper was unchanged at 7.50 percent.
The stock market ended a wild roller-coaster session on Thursday with a modest 0.29 percent gain and an all-time high turnover of T$297 billion (US$10.65 billion).
Dealers said the money rates' movements would depend on whether the central bank stepped in to mop up loose liquidity to dampen the feverish stock market.
The central bank has made several major issues of negotiable certificates of deposit recently but did not do so on Thursday.
Central bank Governor Sheu Yuan-dong said late on Wednesday the bank would not adjust monetary policy merely to cool the bourse, saying money supply was no economic cure-all.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 6.0200 percent against 6.0050.
